en.title: Ț
en.summary: The letter Ț is the twenty-first letter of the Romanian alphabet.

sections.title: Sound of the letter
paragraphs: The name of this letter is pronounced /ts/. Its main sound is the sound /ts/, heard in the word (țară) /ˈtsa.rə/, which means country, land. This letter makes only one sound in standard Romanian.

sections.title: How to say it
paragraphs: Touch the roof of your mouth just behind your upper teeth with your tongue tip. Block the air completely for a moment. Then release the air sharply through a narrow gap while blowing. Your vocal cords do not vibrate. Place your hand on your neck to check that there is no buzzing vibration.

sections.title: Reading and spelling
paragraphs: This letter always produces the same sound in every standard position. You pronounce it as the sound /ts/ whenever you see it written, like in the word (băiat) /bəˈjat/. It does not change before any vowel or consonant.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not soften this consonant into the English sound in ship or chin. It is exactly like the sound in the middle of cats or pizza. Keep the initial stop crisp and release it straight into the hissing air. Never add a trailing breath or vowel at the end.
